aula.titulo: Frases subordinadas 2: wenn, ob and indirect questions
aula.objetivo: Build sentences with «wenn» (if, when), «ob» (whether, in indirect questions) and question words (wo, wann, warum…) in indirect questions, with the verb at the end of the subordinate clause.

itens.enunciado: ___ es regnet, bleibe ich zu Hause. (se)
itens.explicacao: Condition: «wenn».

itens.enunciado: Build the sentence: «Excuse me, could you tell me when the train to Berlin leaves?»

itens.explicacao: Write: Entschuldigung, können Sie mir sagen, wann der Zug nach Berlin abfährt?
Pergunta indireta: «ob».

itens.enunciado: Write 5 sentences: one with «wenn», one with «ob», one with «weil», one with «dass» and one indirect question with «wo» or «wann».
itens.respostaEsperada: Wenn es regnet, bleibe ich zu Hause. Ich weiß nicht, ob er kommt. Ich bleibe, weil ich müde bin. Ich glaube, dass er Zeit hat. Können Sie mir sagen, wann der Zug abfährt?

itens.enunciado: Is there a mistake in this sentence? Correct it or write «OK»: Ich glaube, dass er kommt.

blocos.titulo: The typical mistake of English speakers
blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: The costliest mistake is leaving the verb in the middle: weil ich bin krank. The English ear does not notice anything missing. The second mistake is forgetting the inversion when the subordinate clause opens the sentence: Wenn es regnet, wir bleiben zu Hause. The third is using wenn for everything, as if it were English “when” and “if”: for a single past event, it is als; for a yes/no question, it is ob. STEP 2: Reread the table and say each correct sentence out loud before looking at the reason.

blocos.texto: Can I do it yet? I explain why I do something with weil and send the verb to the end. · I choose between wenn, als and wann. · I turn Wo wohnt er? into Ich weiß nicht, wo er wohnt.

blocos.enunciado: Write 8 sentences, two with each conjunction: weil, dass, wenn and ob.
